chunks: he who is in charge of honour, life, booty, legal commandments and the leadership of the Muslims should not be a miser, as his greed would aim at their wealth,
nor be ignorant as he would then mislead them with his ignorance,
nor be of rude behaviour who would estrange them with his rudeness,
nor should he deal unjustly with wealth thus preferring one group over another,
nor should he accept a bribe while taking decisions, as he would forfeit rights and hold them up without finality,
nor should he ignore sunnah as he would ruin the people.

key_terms.الدِّمَاءِ: Life / Blood (referring to the safeguarding of lives)
key_terms.الْجَائِفُ لِلدُّوَلِ: The one who deals unjustly with wealth
key_terms.الْفُرُوجِ: Honour / Dignity (often referring to life and status)
key_terms.الْمَعَطِّلُ لِلسُّنَّةِ: The one who neglects the Sunnah

ai.seo_question: What are the key character traits a Muslim ruler must avoid according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) delineates the moral and administrative qualifications for leadership, warning against specific vices that corrupt governance. He identifies the miser, the ignorant, the harsh, the partial, the bribe-taker, and the innovator as unfit rulers, linking their personal flaws directly to the spiritual and material welfare of the Ummah. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *'adl* (justice) and *'ilm* (knowledge) as foundational pillars of legitimate authority.

en.sayed-ali-raza: he who is in charge of honour, life, booty (enforcement of), legal commandments and the leardership of the Muslims should not be a miser as his greed would aim at their wealth,
nor be ignorant as he would then mislead there with his ignorance,
nor be of rude behaviour who would estrange them with his rudeness,
nor should he deal unjustly with wealth thus preferring one group over another,
nor should he accept. a bribe while taking decisions, as he would forfeit (others) rights and hold them up without finality,
nor should he ignore sunnah as he would ruin the people.
